title: A GUI must never trigger collection merely by being loaded or launched
requirement: Opening, loading, or launching a Clank's GUI/dashboard MUST NOT, by itself, start a collector run. Collection MUST require an explicit operator action (a button click or equivalent) taken after the GUI is already up, or be driven by a mechanism entirely outside the GUI process (an OS scheduler, a separate daemon) that the GUI does not implicitly trigger.
rationale: Every surveyed Clank with a GUI keeps page-load/launch side-effect-free with respect to collection, and where a violation of this nearly happened it was treated as a production incident, not a style choice: oem-radar's own launcher docstring cites a real 2026-08-27 fleet audit finding where a differently-built kwargs path made the auto_crawl guard raise on every launch, and oem-radar's DashboardConfig.auto_crawl_on_start defaults False specifically to avoid the dashboard becoming an unaccountable production actor, citing clank-architecture's Fleet Law 5 (single scheduling/notification authority per lane). This is independently reasoned, not merely copied text.
forbidden: A GUI process that starts a crawl/collection cycle in its startup/lifespan handler
A GUI whose 'read' routes (GET) have collection side effects
Relying on a config flag defaulting to on for auto-collection-on-launch
acceptance: No GET route or process-startup/lifespan hook initiates a collector run
Every code path that starts a collector run is reachable only from an explicit POST/action triggered after the GUI has already rendered
If a config flag exists to allow launch-time collection, its default is off/false

evidence.summary: 2026-08-27 fleet audit: a launcher-built kwargs path made the auto-crawl guard raise on every launch; fixed by routing through shared build_dashboard_crawl_kwargs and hardcoding the .exe launcher to never auto-crawl.

Fleet Law 5: exactly one enabled scheduling mechanism per Clank-lane; a dashboard that becomes an implicit production actor is an authority leak. Cited directly by oem-radar/src/oem_radar/core/config.py:183-189.
Every surveyed GUI states or structurally shows that launch/page-load never starts a collector; several state this explicitly in a module docstring.

Counter-context, not a violation: smartphone-clank's actual scheduled collection runs in a separate daemon process (APScheduler), architecturally outside the read-only Phase-0 dashboard — consistent with 'not triggered by the GUI', but shows automatic collection does exist elsewhere in the fleet outside a GUI's control.

notes: RATIFIED 2026-08-30 by Operator Ratification Decision 001 (decisions/0003-operator-ratification-decision-001.md), unchanged from the Pass 1 proposal. Scope is deliberately narrow: it governs the GUI process's own behavior, not whether automatic collection may exist elsewhere (a daemon, an OS scheduler) — that is out of scope for a UI standard. See docs/gui-ratification-pass-1.md for the full evidence table.
